active_work_package.title: Platform repository skeleton from the P0.2 design
active_work_package.objective: Create the place every later package lands, shaped so the modular monolith boundaries are tested rather than intended: the workspace and layout, the module registry, the seven dependency rules generated from it, the migration lint, the boundary test suite that proves both fire, the charter, these records and their schemas, and the CI skeleton. It implements no epic and creates no domain table.

stop_reason: An independent peer review of this branch has now returned REVISION_REQUIRED twice. The first pass raised four blockers, closed in commit 3f970e4. The second pass raised three more, and they are closed here. NEW-2: the migration lint modelled TABLE and SCHEMA and silently passed every other DDL verb, so DROP SCHEMA, ALTER ... SET SCHEMA and CREATE VIEW, POLICY, TRIGGER, SEQUENCE, TYPE and FUNCTION against another module's schema all linted clean; it now denies by default. NEW-1: the domain-word stems were anchored, so policyholder walked past a rule whose whole purpose is to stop a P0 domain table; they now match as prefixes, deliberately and with the breadth accepted. NEW-3: the previous round pinned the authority enum in the state file and left badf/authority.yaml, the registry that file mirrors, checked for nothing but a version line, so a review appended a granted_extra: section with two forged grants and the validator returned exit 0; the registry is now parsed, refuses an unknown section and must agree with the state file. Two minor findings are closed too: the M5 not-tenant-owned marker was file-wide and let a table with no tenant_id ride in behind a legitimate one, and an audit column TYPE change had no sub-check of its own. WP-001 stays at ENGINEERING_READY. The reviewer, not the implementer, decides whether a revision closes a finding, and no re-review of this head has happened. The primary action is still NS-001, because negative control 6 remains unobservable until a human records branch protection.
known_divergence: The boundary rules here are the PROPOSAL of a design at IN_REVIEW that depends on five ADRs, all DRAFT_REQUIRED; if ADR-001 narrows or widens the seven rules, the registry and the generator change with it and the suite is re-run. Three lessons from two review rounds are recorded rather than smoothed over. First, the suite was green while four rules were unenforced, which is why scripts/mutation-check.mjs is a required check: a suite that passes whether or not the rule works cannot tell you which it is. Second, a fixture carrying two violations of one rule proves neither, so the migration controls assert on the message rather than the rule name. Third, and this is the round-two lesson, each of the three new blockers was a HOLE BESIDE A FIX rather than a fresh mistake: the domain-word rule was patched for plurals and stayed open to compounds, the authority enum was pinned in the mirror and left open in the source, and the lint was taught the verbs someone thought of and stayed silent on the rest. The response in each case is to invert the default rather than extend the list, which is why the lint now denies by default, the stems match as prefixes and the authority parser refuses an unknown section. Declared non-coverage grew from seven items to twelve after round one and stands at fourteen now; the growth is the point, because the earlier lists were honest in tone and incomplete in fact.
